title: AI, Brain Death Detection, and Islamic Law
abstract: arXiv:2608.16903v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The deployment of machine learning systems capable of detecting covert consciousness in neurologically injured patients creates a profound challenge at the intersection of clinical medicine, AI ethics, and Islamic jurisprudence. We argue that the shift from binary clinical verdicts to probabilistic, temporally granular neural-state estimates should be addressed through three foundational constructs in Islamic legal epistemology: bayyina (clear evidentiary proof), yaqin (epistemic certainty), and the theologically mandated agnosticism about there (soul). We survey the current technical literature on AI-based consciousness detection, map it onto the landscape of Islamic brain death scholarship, and identifykey challenges. We also discuss its implications for AI surrogate decision systems.

translated_title: 人工智能、脑死亡检测与伊斯兰法
translated_abstract: 摘要：能够检测神经损伤患者隐性意识的机器学习系统的部署，在临床医学、人工智能伦理和伊斯兰法理学交汇处提出了深刻挑战。我们认为，从二元临床判定转向概率性、时间粒度的神经状态估计，应通过伊斯兰法律认识论中的三个基本构造来处理：bayyina（明确证据证明）、yaqin（认知确定性）以及关于灵魂（ruh）的神学规定的不可知论。我们综述了当前基于人工智能的意识检测技术文献，将其映射到伊斯兰脑死亡学术领域，并识别关键挑战。我们还讨论了其对人工智能代理决策系统的影响。
tldr: 本文探讨了AI意识检测系统在伊斯兰法框架下的伦理与法律挑战，提出通过伊斯兰法律认识论的三个核心概念来应对从二元判定到概率性神经状态评估的转变。
en_tdlr: This paper explores the ethical and legal challenges of AI-based consciousness detection within Islamic jurisprudence, proposing three foundational Islamic legal concepts to address the shift from binary verdicts to probabilistic neural-state estimates.
